First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-18t+27)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+27t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(3)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(3)^{3}-9(3)^{2}+27(3)+C \\ 0 & =27-81+81+C \\ C & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+27t-27=(t-3)^{3}.$

To find the time interval in which the particle is moving to the *right*, we must solve the inequality $v>0.$ This gives

$$
(t-3)^{3}>0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t),$ we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094087/assets/e36c5ac354bfca5db21249d75862731c028e9f771da9070aa3382c033975e412.png)

From the graph, we see that $v>0$ whenever $t>3.$
